answer: An oasis market for opal should reject a plume of complaints from invented customers. Only a buyer key named in a settled, signed order may open a dispute, and a shared docket allows one case per order ID. Key rotation preserves that case history; appeals update the same record instead of creating fresh claims. Thousands of aliases cannot turn one purchase into thousands of freezes on a seller. Additional cases require additional genuine orders. This limits Sybil harassment, though well-funded buyers can still purchase many orders and legitimate disputes need fair review.
